_note: Font-pairing catalog. The Designer picks a named pairing for the chosen theme (see themes.json `type` directions) and records it; the Programmer wires the stacks into --font-display / --font-body / --font-ui (or --font-mono) in :root. Every stack here is self-contained and offline-capable. Pick ONE display + ONE body + at most ONE ui/mono per story.
_license_note: Font stacks adapted from system-fonts/modern-font-stacks (CC0-1.0, github.com/system-fonts/modern-font-stacks). Ban list + pairing/contrast rules adapted from anthropic/claude-cookbooks aesthetics notebook (MIT). Font family names are nominative references to the typefaces themselves; no font binaries are bundled by this file.
principle: Page runs on file://; casual Google-Fonts calls fail silently offline. Default to tier-1 system or tier-2 web-safe stacks; tier-3 embedded webfont only when subsetted + self-hosted.
avoid_reason: These read as templated defaults (the generic-AI look in themes.json anti_patterns). Inter/Roboto/Open Sans/Lato/Space Grotesk are over-shipped; Arial as the primary face signals an unstyled page; one system font for everything flattens the display/body/UI hierarchy this catalog exists to create.

tier1_system._note: Fonts already installed on common OSes — zero network, instant render, no embedding. First choice. Each pairing lists the full fallback stack to drop verbatim into the CSS variable.

broadsheet.display: Charter, 'Bitstream Charter', 'Sitka Text', Cambria, Georgia, serif
broadsheet.body: Charter, 'Bitstream Charter', 'Sitka Text', Cambria, Georgia, serif
broadsheet.subject: investigative / policy / serious analysis; reportage-led stories

tufte_reader.body: 'Iowan Old Style', 'Palatino Linotype', 'URW Palladio L', P052, Georgia, serif

didone_fashion.note: Didone display is thin-stroked — reserve for large sizes (h1/h2) and pair with a sturdier body (Georgia) for running text.

modern_desk.mono: ui-monospace, 'Cascadia Code', 'Source Code Pro', Menlo, Consolas, monospace
modern_desk.subject: quant rankings, benchmarks, structured data; UI-forward layouts
modern_desk.note: Use the `system-ui` keyword for the sans display — NOT Inter/Roboto as a named primary. Roboto appears here only as a late Android fallback inside the system stack.

field_report.body: Charter, 'Bitstream Charter', 'Sitka Text', Cambria, Georgia, serif

tier2_websafe.palatino: 'Palatino Linotype', Palatino, 'Book Antiqua', URW Palladio L, serif
tier2_websafe.baskerville: Baskerville, 'Baskerville Old Face', 'Hoefler Text', Garamond, 'Times New Roman', serif
tier2_websafe.mono: ui-monospace, 'Cascadia Code', 'Source Code Pro', Menlo, Consolas, 'DejaVu Sans Mono', monospace

tier3_embedded_webfont.strategy: Embed AT MOST one subsetted woff2 as a base64 @font-face with font-display:swap and a full fallback stack. Use only when the brand face genuinely carries the story and no tier-1/tier-2 stack matches; otherwise stay on system fonts.
tier3_embedded_webfont.recipe: 1) Pick ONE face (usually the display). 2) Subset to the glyphs actually used (latin + the digits/punctuation in headlines) with fonttools/pyftsubset or glyphhanger -> woff2. 3) base64-encode the woff2 and inline it: @font-face{font-family:'X';src:url(data:font/woff2;base64,AAAA...) format('woff2');font-display:swap;font-weight:...;} 4) Reference it FIRST in the variable with a tier-1/tier-2 fallback after it: --font-display:'X', Georgia, serif; so text renders immediately on the fallback and swaps when the face decodes.
tier3_embedded_webfont.tradeoff: base64 adds ~33% over the binary size and is render-blocking parse weight inside the HTML; keep the subset to ~5KB (display-only, one weight). Never inline a full multi-weight family. If two faces are tempting, drop to a tier-1 pairing instead.
tier3_embedded_webfont.note: These are recommendations ONLY for when you can self-host/subset; do NOT pull them from Google Fonts at runtime (the call fails silently on file://).

type_rules._note: Contrast rules from the cookbook aesthetics notebook — apply on top of design_tokens.json type_scale.
type_rules.weight_extremes: Use weight extremes for contrast (100/200 vs 800/900), not 400 vs 600. A light display over a heavy stat number reads as deliberate; adjacent mid-weights read as accidental.
type_rules.size_jumps: Make size jumps 3x+, not 1.5x. h1 should tower over body; a timid 1.5x step looks like a mistake rather than a hierarchy.
type_rules.high_contrast_pairings: Pair across categories for tension: serif display + geometric/mono UI, or expressive sans display + serif body. Two faces from the same category (two grotesks, two transitionals) muddy rather than contrast.
type_rules.one_of_each: One display family, one body family, one UI/mono family at most (echoes design_tokens.json). The catalog's job is to choose those three deliberately, not to add a fourth.

choosing: Read the chosen theme's `type` direction in themes.json, then pick the named tier-1 pairing it points to (e.g. field_report, broadsheet, didone_fashion). Drop the stacks into :root as --font-display / --font-body / --font-ui (or --font-mono). Record the pairing name in designer.json page_rhythm so the Programmer wires the same stacks the Designer chose.
